The condition-coercion audit corrects four renv RY001 identities previously labeled true_positive in upstream-package: R/bootstrap.R:800:7, R/cache.R:538:7, and inst/resources/activate.R:16:7 and :960:9, at pin a3f8952cf8f4b9cd6e676805431cb81ca5a24b64. Each tests a scalar Sys.getenv result with unset="FALSE" or "TRUE". R accepts these strings in if conditions; an unknown user value is not proof of an invalid condition. Exact pinned assignment/condition probes accept defaults and TRUE/FALSE while garbage raises the expected error. The four labels were therefore false positives under the uncertainty policy, not unconditional runtime errors. This rule does not guarantee arbitrary environment values are valid. Full pinned comparison removes exactly these four identities, adds none, and retains every other finding. Proven invalid literals remain tested by the condition-coercion fixtures.

Function-mode call-head lookup removes four RY070 identities. rlang tests/testthat/helper-locale.R:134:5 called skip() past a local logical skip; R resolves the head to testthat::skip (probe: with testthat attached the call raises testthat's skip control condition, never an error), so the prior true_positive label -- assigned in the audit batch documented in docs/corpus/pre-governance-measurement.md with the ordinary-lookup rationale "a local logical skip shadows the function" -- was a mislabel and the finding was a false positive. pkgdown tests/testthat/helper.R:24-26 called path() past the NULL formal of local_pkgdown_site; pkgdown's NAMESPACE import(fs) binds fs::path, and R's function-mode lookup skips the NULL formal (probe: fs::path runs); their recorded false_positive labels were correct. All other identities are unchanged, including pkgdown R/templates.R:57:5, which still fires because import(fs) is not enumerable hermetically (fs ships no stub; issue #366); its true_positive label was assigned with the same shadowing rationale and is flagged to the maintainers for review under function-mode semantics, not relabeled here. Remaining RY070 messages gain the function-mode wording.

Audit correction: pkgdown R/templates.R:57:5 RY070 was labeled true_positive in the pre-governance audit batch with the ordinary-lookup rationale 'a local path <- NULL shadows the function'. R's call-head lookup is function-mode: in a namespace-faithful evaluation of the exact pinned function (pkgdown 179cfaee3d4e, templates_dir), with NAMESPACE import(fs) bindings and template.path/template.package unset, line 57 resolves past the local NULL binding to fs::path and returns an fs_path; a base-only negative control errors 'could not find function path' (R 4.6.1; evidence scripts in the review record). The finding is a false positive at package runtime. The diagnostic still fires hermetically because fs ships no embedded stub (issue #366); the record, audit group, reports, and messages are unchanged and the finding remains emitted - only the label and derived classification counts change (true_positive 42->41, false_positive 486->487; totals, identities, and source_sha256 unchanged).

RY109 (self-referential-default, issue #364) adds 25 reviewed findings. 23 true positives, each runtime-verified as a default naming its own formal (or calling a same-named function, which the formal shadowing makes equivalent) that can only resolve to its own promise and can never evaluate; forcing the promise errors with R's 'promise already under evaluation'. Most identities were verified to error on a triggering call; dplyr R/distinct.R:81 and dbplyr R/verb-distinct.R:61 (`caller_env = caller_env(2)`: the formal is never consumed, so the call runs when it is missing) and ggplot2 R/stat-bindot.R:133 (`method = method`: unused in the body; `densitybin(1:3)` runs) were verified as dead-on-arrival defaults that would error the moment anyone consumed them. The flagged shapes are the dtplyr shipped bug (fixed upstream in dbe32a6), callee-named defaults whose formal shadows a real function (purrr caller_env(), httr config(), pkgdown error_call(), dplyr/dbplyr caller_env(2)), closure-capture misconceptions where the author meant an outer variable but the formal shadows it (gt data_tbl/col_classes/data, pkgdown pkg, sparklyr master/config), and eagerly-forwarded bare self-references (ellmer type, infer/parsnip call, shiny width/height, ggplot2 method/method.args, lubridate tz(x)/.select_formats). All are latent at the pinned commits: current callers supply the formals. The two false positives are rlang's own defusing tests (test-nse-defuse.R:329,334): bare enexpr/enquo defined by rlang itself cannot be credited as defusers without provenance (crediting a project-defined name would also credit a test-local `quote <- function(x) x`, which forces), so ry warns on the deliberate idiom; warning severity keeps that cost low. Deliberate defusing elsewhere stays silent through typeshed captures_promise/quoted_expression provenance or {{ }} injection recognition (corrr, dbplyr sql_runif); two suppression-side false negatives (defuse-then-force, divergent branches) are pinned as oracle known-gap fixtures.

Superassignment modeling (#374) removes 11 false positives, all traced to bindings mutated only through `<<-` in nested closures. pak R/json.R loses all ten RY001s on `token` (4 reassign-scope: lines 81, 83, 98, 135 are the `if (token == ...)`/`while (token != ...)` conditions of parse_value/parse_object/parse_array around `token <- NULL` + `token <<- tokens[ptr]`/`'EOF'` in read_token; 6 type-narrowing: lines 100, 108, 118, 120, 141, 143 are the sibling token conditions in the same walkers) -- the vendored r-json-parser shape whose loops run correctly at the pin (cdbd4ce, verified in R). flexdashboard R/flex_dashboard.R:381 is `!file.exists(source_file)` where `source_file <- NULL` is overwritten by `source_file <<- input` in pre_knit: the stale NULL made file.exists logical(0); the five reassign-scope removals (four pak, one flexdashboard) take that audit group from 9 to 4. Every removal is the conservative unknown-typed update applied at the <<-writing definition; no new identity appeared. The sibling write-side shapes stay: dplyr summarise.R:342 / blogdown serve.R / reticulate wrapper.R bind through plain `<-` in call-argument closures or textConnection dynamic bindings (#350 family), not `<<-`.

RY111 (constant-argument-shadowing, issue #361) adds 20 reviewed findings: 17 true positives and 3 false positives. The true positives are the dbplyr sql_render.*_query family (own `subquery` formal never read while the generic forwards the caller's flag into the method), reticulate's r_to_py.POSIXt (the method POSIXct/POSIXlt dispatch to) and r_convert_dataframe_column (their `convert` contract parameter is never read; every internal import/r_to_py_impl call is pinned `convert = FALSE`), shiny's observeEvent (`autoDestroy = TRUE` pinned while label/suspended/priority/domain are all forwarded), and torch's nnf_rrelu_ (`training = TRUE` forced against the method's own `training = FALSE` default). The false positives are deliberate compat surfaces: gt's testthat helpers expose `all = TRUE` signatures that mirror expect_match while always matching all fragments, and sparklyr's stream_read_socket exposes the stream_read_* family's `columns` argument that the socket source cannot use. The dead-formal gate silences the deliberate idioms the ungated name-match would flag (forwarded `subquery`/`quiet`, guarded `ignore_case`/`recursive`, read `inherit`).
